campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution to authorize a funding agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority for a low-carbon transportation program supporting transit reliability and performance improvements. The agenda also touched on pothole damage and the process for filing related claims.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize funding agreement with VTA for the Low Carbon Transportation and Operations Program
Transit reliability improvement and performance systems project
Pothole damage and claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up routine business including meeting minutes, check registers, and the Treasurer's Report, along with responses to two Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of the BART Silicon Valley Phase II project. The Council also considered a state bill on utility data transparency, a contract for a transportation impact fee study, forming a committee to review alternative policing services, the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival, and the city's continued involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Civil Grand Jury responses on pothole damage claims and VTA's management of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a bill on utility data transparency related to power charge calculations
$85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
Future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued participation in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine budget and contract items, including updated pay schedules for city employee groups and additional funding for an electrical maintenance contractor. The Council also considered renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street, restructuring the Volunteer Awards Committee, and a citizen initiative on zoning impacts, along with discussions on the Environmental Commission and upcoming CalCities conference votes.
keyTopics: Resolution to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street
Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee associations and management staff
Amendment No. 4 to increase the Bear Electrical Solutions maintenance contract by $250,000
Disbanding the Joint Volunteer Awards Committee and forming a Los Altos-only version
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council met to approve routine meeting minutes and take up a handful of other items, including vacating a public service easement on Cerro Vista, setting up new preferential and time-limited parking rules, and hiring a consultant to help with an executive-level search or process.
keyTopics: Vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-related services
Approval of minutes from several August 2026 Council meetings

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 9, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming September 15 and September 22, 2026 City Council agendas, including whether to add items or set specific discussion times. The committee also considered routine reports, a mayoral travel request, and a proposal from several council members regarding transparency and private non-disclosure agreements.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 15, 2026 Council agenda
Review of the September 22, 2026 draft Council agenda
City Clerk's public record report for August 27–September 3, 2026
City Auditor's monthly activity report for August 2026
Proposal on Council transparency and private non-disclosure agreements

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — September 14, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to take public comments, do a team-building activity, and discuss its proposed work plan for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Members also shared committee updates and reviewed upcoming meeting agendas from other city boards and commissions.
keyTopics: Public oral communications on non-agenda items
Team-building exercise for committee members
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's Fiscal Year 2026-27 work plan
Committee and staff comments, questions, and reports
Review of agendas from other city boards, commissions, and committees

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session, received a presentation on the Clean Water Program, and then took up a regular meeting agenda covering routine business, contract and purchasing approvals, and a Caltrain budget update. The Council also reviewed progress on its multi-year strategic workplan.
keyTopics: Clean Water Program update presented by staff
Library materials handling system purchase order for the Main Library, not to exceed about $635,000
Side letter with the Communication Officer's Association and related updates to job classifications and salary resolution
Caltrain budget update presented by Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board Chief of Staff Casey Fromson
Year 1 update on the Council's Strategic Workplan

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — September 9, 2026
cupertino.summary: This meeting kicked off the new 2026-2028 term for Cupertino's Teen Commission, starting with the swearing-in of newly appointed commissioners and an orientation session. The Commission also considered selecting its Chair and Vice Chair for 2026-2027 and discussed potential meeting topics for the year ahead, along with a presentation on teen programs.
keyTopics: Swearing-in of incoming 2026-2028 Teen Commissioners
Teen Commission orientation for new members
Presentation on teen programs
Selection of 2026-2027 Chair and Vice Chair
Discussion of Teen Commission meeting topics for 2026-2027

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council held a special meeting that included interviews and appointments for two openings on the Civil Service Commission, followed by a joint session with the Stadium Authority Board. The joint meeting covered recognitions for outgoing board and commission members and campaign sponsors, along with several routine business items including a janitorial services contract amendment, a historic preservation agreement, and board/commission annual workplans.
keyTopics: Interviews and appointments to fill two Civil Service Commission seats (partial term to 2028, full term to 2030)
Recognition of outgoing commissioners from the Library Trustees, Civil Service, Cultural, Historical and Landmarks, Parks and Recreation, and Senior Advisory boards
Recognition of 2026 Mission Meets the Moment campaign sponsors
Authorization to negotiate and execute amendments to the citywide janitorial services agreement with Impec Group, Inc.
A Mills Act historic preservation agreement for the property at 1261 Jackson Street

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: This meeting of the Successor Agency to the former Redevelopment Agency of Milpitas dealt with administrative and financial housekeeping. The Council, acting as the Successor Agency Board, considered confirming which city officials hold official positions with the Successor Agency and considered authorizing the sale of refunding bonds tied to old redevelopment debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance existing redevelopment-related debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — September 9, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council's Planning & Transportation Commission considered a proposed ordinance change to city rules governing the separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The meeting also included a routine director's report, discussion of the meeting schedule and commission assignments, and approval of prior meeting minutes.
keyTopics: Proposed ordinance amending Municipal Code Titles 18 and 21 regarding separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs)
Director's report covering department updates
Discussion of meeting schedule and commission assignments
Approval of Planning & Transportation Commission draft minutes from August 12, 2026
